newsitem.title: USA: Fannie, Freddie off on growth concerns - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Fannie, Freddie off on growth concerns - analyst.

text.p: Fannie Mae and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (Freddie Mac) were lower on concerns about growth rates, analyst Jonathan Gray of Sanford C. Bernstein Co said Friday.

Gray said banks and thrifts have been holding fixed-rate loans rather than securitizing them, despite the interest rate risk. When banks and thrifts keep the paper, the volume going to the government agencies Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is reduced. Both Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are government-sponsored corporations which buy mortgages and then sell them through securitization.
The analyst said while the trend has been in evidence for months, investors have reacted only recently.
Gray said he has both stocks rated outperform. He added, "even on lower growth rate assumptions, the stocks appear to be moderately undervalued."
Fannie Mae was off 1-13/16 to 42-3/4 in early afternoon. Freddie Mac was off 1-11/16 to 32.
